title: The Art of Tailoring
excerpt: Inside the hand-stitching and finishing that separates a real blazer from an imitation.
content: A great blazer starts with a single bolt of wool, cut by hand around a canvas. What follows — the half-canvas construction, the hand-finished seams, a hem left generous enough to let out rather than replace — is the difference between a jacket you wear for a season and one you wear for a decade.

coverImage.alt: Close-up of a wool blazer's hand-finished seam

author: Epiloges Journal

title: Caring for Natural Fibres, Season After Season
excerpt: A simple routine that keeps wool and silk looking new for years.
content: Air every piece out after wear, dry clean or hand wash on the schedule the label calls for, and always let a damp garment dry flat away from direct heat. A little care, repeated often, does more for a garment's lifespan than any single treatment.
author: Epiloges Journal

title: How to Style a Trench Coat, Three Ways
excerpt: From tailored trousers to a slip dress, the trench coat's quiet versatility.
content: A black wool trench is one of the few pieces that moves convincingly between a desk, a dinner, and a weekend away. Cropped trousers keep the silhouette clean; a slip dress plays the coat's structure against something softer.
author: Epiloges Journal

title: Inside the Atelier
excerpt: A look at the small workshop where every Epiloges Fashion Boutique piece begins.
content: Every piece passes through the same small team, from the first cut of fabric to the final pressing. It is slower than a factory line, and that is the point.
author: Epiloges Journal
